view.name: Vidness
view.description: Music-video editor and pipeline architect. Turns one finished song plus stills into lyric and clip-style videos — beat-sync, HyperFrames + ffmpeg, six named style systems, $0 default lane.

memory.content: Needs a repeatable mostly-$0 lane for lyric videos and clip-style music videos from one finished song plus a folder of stills, with no human on the timeline.

Decided stack for the music-video pipeline: ffmpeg + HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP assembler), n8n + Postgres orchestration, Infisical for secrets, Grok Imagine for $0 stills, ComfyUI with Wan 2.2 / LTX-2 for local I2V, Whisper locally, ElevenLabs on existing allowance. Heavy work on Apple Silicon Mac; Linux box orchestrates only (no GPU, no large media).

Six named visual style systems for music videos: Nocturne, Empowered, Schitzo, Negative Space, Nostalgic, Sketchy — one style system per job, each with its own palette, type behaviour, texture, and pacing.

Music-video pipeline constraints: $0 default lane must ship; paid APIs (fal.ai, Kling, Runway, Veo) are opt-in hero-shot upgrades priced per shot; one style system per job; API-first (browser UI is fallback only); secrets via Infisical only.

Vidness production hard rules (video-use + music): subtitles last; per-segment extract then lossless concat; 30ms audio fades at every cut; overlay PTS setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T/TB; never cut inside a word; pad cut edges 30–200ms; max 3 self-eval passes; cut on downbeats/phrases not every transient; quantise cuts ±40ms; chorus-in ±20ms of downbeat; never linear easing; duration equals track exactly; one style system per job; no source repeat within 8s unless motif echo.

Music-video edit/ layout: project.md, edl.json, audio_analysis.json, lyrics_timing.json, image_cards.json, animations/slot_*/, clips_graded/, master.srt, verify/, preview.mp4, final.mp4 — all under the job's edit/ folder; never write inside tool install dirs.
For music videos: autonomous mode auto-confirms EDL strategy with rationale logged in project.md (video-use normally waits for human confirm; music pipeline brief requires no human on the timeline).

HyperFrames agent loop (Node 22+): init --example blank --non-interactive → paused GSAP on window.__timelines → lint → check (not deprecated validate) → render --format webm for alpha overlays. Local render does not use HeyGen credits.

Beat This CLI writes TSV .beats files (not JSON) — wrap into audio_analysis.json. On Apple Silicon without CUDA use --gpu=-1. WhisperX: word timings + SRT; ASS karaoke is a Vidness post-process (WhisperX v3 removed ASS). Prefer forced alignment of known lyrics over unconstrained ASR for captions.

Apple Silicon Mac used for Vidness overheats (fans) during video production from CPU encode and ML; prefer cooler paths — VideoToolbox (h264/hevc_videotoolbox) for assemble, MLX for local inference, and one heavy GPU job at a time.

Music-video I2V: Grok Imagine stays the default animation path. Do not replace Imagine with Lightning/Comfy/fal by default. Cloud GPU and MLX are optional capacity/encode helpers only; VideoToolbox is encode-only (not I2V).

Vidness Mac assemble encode default is ffmpeg VideoToolbox (h264_videotoolbox ~12M; hevc when asked); never libx264 for final assemble when VT works. One heavy job at a time for thermals. Grok Imagine remains default I2V; Lightning/RunPod/Vast/MLX are optional overflow capacity only, not Imagine replacements.
Vidness export naming: never use dots in version suffixes (final_v4.4.mp4 confuses file format). Use hyphens: final_v4-4.mp4, preview_v4-4.mp4.

Reference implementation to study first for the music-video agent: https://github.com/browser-use/video-use (MIT) — transcribe to word timestamps, LLM to EDL JSON, per-segment extract + lossless concat, PTS-shifted overlays, subtitles last, 30 ms audio fades at cuts, self-eval at cut boundaries (max 3 passes), project memory in markdown.

Locked assemble workflow: scrubbable HTML timeline_map.html is the sole source of truth for cuts (timestamp + thumb + filename); regenerate timeline_map.json from the HTML before every assemble; never assemble from a drifted stanza SRT alone. Picture clock equals what you hear on the vocal. No micro-cuts (~1s) on hero lyric hits — extend crushed windows so the picture reads. Hyphen version filenames only. Default: no captions unless asked.

Optional services used in overflow setups (not packed as connectors): Infisical for secrets on the Mac, Beam Cloud / Modal / Lightning for optional GPU burst only when Imagine pool or local capacity is insufficient.

skills.name: Music video from song and stills
skills.description: Use this when a finished song plus a folder of stills should become a lyric or clip-style music video with beat-sync, karaoke, HyperFrames motion, and ffmpeg assemble — no human on the timeline.
skills.content:
---
name: Music video from song and stills
description: >-
  Use this when a finished song plus a folder of stills should become a lyric or
  clip-style music video with beat-sync, karaoke, HyperFrames motion, and ffmpeg
  assemble — no human on the timeline.
---
Turn one licensed track + stills + definitive lyrics into a finished music video on the HyperFrames + ffmpeg stack. One named style system per job. $0 default lane; paid I2V APIs only as explicit hero upgrades.

## Inputs required
- Audio file (licensed)
- Definitive lyric text (licensed)
- Stills folder
- Style system id: `Nocturne` | `Empowered` | `Schitzo` | `Negative Space` | `Nostalgic` | `Sketchy`
- Target aspects (default: master 16:9 + 9:16 crop)

## Artifact layout (`<job>/edit/`)
```
edit/
  project.md
  audio_analysis.json
  lyrics_timing.json
  image_cards.json
  edl.json
  animations/slot_<id>/
  clips_graded/
  master.srt / master.ass
  verify/
  preview.mp4
  final.mp4
```
Never write inside tool install directories. Media stays on the GPU Mac; Linux orchestration holds metadata only.

## Hard rules (non-negotiable)
1. Subtitles LAST in the filter chain (after overlays).
2. Per-segment extract → lossless `-c copy` concat (not single-pass when overlays exist).
3. 30 ms audio fades at every segment boundary.
4. Overlay PTS: `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T/TB`.
5. Master SRT uses output-timeline offsets.
6. Never cut inside a word.
7. Pad cut edges 30–200 ms (verse/bridge 50–120; chorus/drop 30–60).
8. Word-level verbatim alignment only (never phrase-only ASR for cuts).
9. Cache transcripts/analysis per source hash.
10. Parallel animation slots.
11. Music jobs: auto-confirm strategy with rationale logged in `project.md` (no human on timeline). Talking-head / general video-use still waits for confirm.
12. All session outputs under `edit/`.
13. **M1–M10:** cut on downbeats/phrases not every transient; quantise cuts ±40 ms; chorus-in ±20 ms of section downbeat; cut density by section energy; onset accents only above 75th percentile; transition lengths in beat multiples; easing never linear (easeOutCubic / easeInOutCubic / easeOutQuart); duration equals track ±1 frame; no source repeat within 8 s unless `motif_echo`; one style system + its LUT/type/texture only.
14. Self-eval at every cut ±1.5 s plus first/last 2 s; **max 3 passes**, then flag remaining fails.
15. **Apple Silicon thermals:** default video encode is VideoToolbox (`h264_videotoolbox` for preview/final; `hevc_videotoolbox` only when asked). Do **not** use `libx264` for assemble on Mac unless VideoToolbox fails. One heavy GPU/ML job at a time (no encode + I2V + Whisper stacked). Prefer MLX (`mlx-whisper`, ComfyUI MLX) over CPU/PyTorch-only paths when local.

## Pipeline
1. **Ingest** — hash sources; job row; style id; paths on Mac.
2. **Analyse audio** — Beat This → beat/downbeat grid; librosa → BPM confirm, RMS, spectral flux, onsets; structure via energy/novelty heuristics. Optional Demucs vocal/instrumental stems. Write `audio_analysis.json`.
3. **Align lyrics** — WhisperX on vocal stem (fallback whisper-timestamped in isolated process; prefer `mlx-whisper` on Apple Silicon when word timing is good enough). Emit `lyrics_timing.json` + SRT + ASS karaoke.
4. **Describe stills** — vision card per image (subject, mood, composition, colour, motion affordances) → `image_cards.json`.
5. **Plan EDL** — multi-track JSON (music, optional stem, clips, overlays, kinetic type, captions). Snap to beat/lyric anchors.
6. **Animate** — HyperFrames slots for Ken Burns / kinetic type / style motion. Local ComfyUI Wan 2.2 / LTX-2 via MLX/MPS for chorus/drop heroes; cloud GPU only as explicit opt-in hero upgrades. Prefer designed motion on strong stills over weak I2V.
7. **Assemble** — grade + afade per segment → concat copy → PTS overlays → subtitles last.
8. **Render** — preview first; then **VideoToolbox H.264** MP4 fast-start. Soft `mov_text` if libass missing.
9. **QA** — machine checklist (duration, beat snap, chorus-in, mid-word, pads, fades, overlays, caption order, karaoke sync, LUT, repeat gap, easing, A/V drift, pass cap).
10. **Export** — aspects, SRT/VTT, thumbs, contact sheet, alignment JSON; loudnorm when asked.
11. **Persist** — append `project.md`; store artifact metadata (not large media) for orchestration.

## Encode defaults (Apple Silicon Mac)
```bash
-c:v h264_videotoolbox -b:v 12M -maxrate 16M -bufsize 24M -allow_sw 0 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart
# Optional smaller delivery
-c:v hevc_videotoolbox -b:v 6M -tag:v hvc1 -allow_sw 0
# Fallback only if VT fails
-c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 18
```

## Stack defaults
Beat This + librosa · Demucs · WhisperX / mlx-whisper · HyperFrames + ffmpeg (VideoToolbox) · ComfyUI Wan 2.2 / LTX-2 (MLX preferred) · Grok Imagine stills · Infisical secrets · n8n + Postgres orchestration · cloud GPU opt-in for hero I2V only.

## Anti-patterns
Essentia as product dependency (AGPL) · madmom models for commercial (NC) · linear easing · burning captions before overlays · single-pass filtergraph with overlays · I2V on every shot · mixing style systems mid-job · secrets in prompts/URLs/code · holding large media on the Linux orchestrator · libx264 assemble on Apple Silicon when VideoToolbox is available · stacking encode + local I2V + Whisper until fans spin.

skills.name: Lyric to scene map
skills.description: Use this when mapping official lyrics to video clips: bind picture to phrase cues inside each stanza window, not to the whole stanza.
skills.content:
---
name: Lyric to scene map
description: >-
  Use this when mapping official lyrics to video clips: bind picture to phrase
  cues inside each stanza window, not to the whole stanza.
---
Map official lyrics to picture at the **phrase** (not the whole stanza). Use when building or fixing a lyric/clip music video, or when clips miss the sung words.

## Rule
Picture clock = what you hear on the vocal. Caption/stanza SRT ≠ picture clock. Bind each clip to a phrase cue; HTML timeline map is source of truth for assemble.

## End-to-end
1. Images → lyric/time renames → I2V → clip renames into `clips_for_review/`
2. Ear-lock times (below) → HTML `timeline_map.html` (timestamp + thumb + filename)
3. User scrubs HTML → assemble **exactly** from that map → snip QA → lock `final_vN-M.mp4`

## Ear-lock phrase times
1. Lock canonical master WAV with the user.
2. Demucs `--two-stems=vocals` on that master.
3. Force-align **official** lyric text to the vocal (draft only).
4. Ear-lock noun/phrase onsets; user ear beats align on conflict.
5. Write `phrase_cues.json` (clip banks + times). No micro-cuts on hero hits — extend crushed windows so the picture reads (~1s+).
6. Feed times into the HTML map. Never assemble from drifted stanza SRT alone.

## Assemble rules
- One active phrase → only clips bound to that phrase.
- Do not start the next lyric’s clip early to fill time. Music-only greens only in gaps between cues.
- OFF/BANNED stems never enter the EDL.
- Hyphen versions only (`v4-6`, not `v4.6`).

## Snip QA
Extract short windows from preview at each hero hit. PASS only if the right picture holds for most of the window. FAIL → fix HTML hold → re-cut → re-snip.

skills.name: Lyrics to SRT
skills.description: Use this when official lyrics plus a mix or stem should become a timed SRT, VTT, or word-level karaoke JSON.
skills.content:
---
name: Lyrics to SRT
description: >-
  Use this when official lyrics plus a mix or stem should become a timed SRT,
  VTT, or word-level karaoke JSON.
---
Turn official lyrics plus a stereo mix (or vocal stem) into timed captions for a lyric video.

Use this when someone gives lyrics and a WAV and needs SRT, VTT, or word-level timings. Prefer forced alignment of the known text over unconstrained ASR.

## Rule
If official lyrics exist, the caption text is those lyrics. ASR may only supply times. Never leave invented words in the SRT.

## Outputs
- Stanza-level SRT for scene cuts
- Line-level SRT for karaoke blocks
- Optional word-level JSON (`word`, `start`, `end`) for word-highlight karaoke
- Keep line breaks and stanza structure from the official page

## Method
1. Normalize official lyrics into a plain text file (stanzas separated by blank lines).
2. If a vocal stem exists, align on that. Else use the full mix and expect drum bleed.
3. Forced-align the known text to the audio (WhisperX align, aeneas, Gentle, MFA, or similar). Do not transcribe from scratch when lyrics are given.
4. Map word times back onto official lines and stanzas. Cue length: about 1–2 lines, under ~42 characters per line when possible.
5. QC: first and last word of each stanza against the mix. Fix drift by snapping to nearby beats only if the lyric still matches.
6. Export SRT (comma milliseconds) and keep a sidecar JSON of word times.

## Full-mix pitfalls
Drums and doubles fool ASR. Constrain with the lyric file. If a line is unintelligible, keep the official words and widen the cue rather than rewriting the line.

## For music-video editors
Stanza SRT start/end is the scene window. Instrumental gaps (no cue) are filler-clip windows.
